conviction_note: Three unpriced items, all net positive, summing to +3.1: an entire country's advertising operation being closed with no RNS and no UK coverage, a break-up activist crossing 9% in a TR-1 published AFTER the close that sets the entry price, and a buyback that terminated seven days before the print with the Board on record wanting a bigger one. I emit +2.4 rather than +3.1 because the Australia item is genuinely two-sided -- a first-time regulated disclosure of a closure with exceptional cash costs can be sold at 07:00 as easily as it can be bought -- and because the 20d/5d run-up is already mildly positive, so I am not fully independent of the drift.

findings.finding: On 9 September 2026 M+C Saatchi announced that the Parc-backed management buyout of its Australia and New Zealand advertising agency had failed due diligence and that the business will instead CEASE OPERATIONS before the end of 2026, with the entire ANZ leadership team and all staff departing and Woolworths finishing in November. There is no RNS on the subject -- not for the 22 July MBO agreement and not for the 9 September collapse and closure -- and no UK financial outlet has covered it. The 22 September interim statement is the first regulated document in which the UK market can see it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Australia has been the line that moves this stock. The 18 Sep 2025 interims, which carried the Australian restructure and the closure of the Bohemia media unit, produced -12.24% -- by far the largest of the 13 observed reactions (median |move| 1.98%). The 24 Nov 2025 trading update, which downgraded the FY25 decline to 7%, produced -5.16%. But the 20 Apr 2026 FY results, which disclosed FY25 separately-disclosed items of GBP9.1m 'largely restructuring costs in Australia' alongside the language 'simplify the businesses ... unlock the intrinsic value', produced +3.91%. So this line has moved the stock hard in both directions, and the sign has tracked whether Australia was presented as a continuing problem or as a problem being removed. This time it is being removed entirely.
findings.original_quote: M+C Saatchi Group has today announced that, following an extensive review of strategic options for its Australia and New Zealand advertising agency, the previously announced management buyout of the business, backed by private equity, will not proceed, and as a result, M+C Saatchi's advertising arm will cease operations in Australia and NZ before the end of the year. ... The leadership team of Dani Bassil (CEO), Simon Wassef (Chief Strategy Officer), Jeremy Hogg (Executive Creative Director), Anita Zanesco (Chief Client Officer), Remi Couzelas (Managing Director, Re) and Jack Playfair (Head of Sport and Entertainment) will all depart, along with all staff.
findings.why_not_priced: The Investegate RNS record for M&C Saatchi from 1 July 2026 to 21 September 2026 contains nothing but Transaction in Own Shares, three Holding(s) in Company and the Notice of Half Year Results -- no announcement of the MBO, none of its collapse, none of the closure. Every outlet carrying it is Australian trade press (Campaign Brief, Campaign Brief NZ, Campaign Brief Asia, Mumbrella, Mediaweek, B&T, Mi3). Sharecast covered this issuer's March 2026 CEO change, so it follows the name, and it did not carry this. If the market had priced the closure of an entire country's advertising operations announced with no consideration and all staff departing, the stock would not be sitting at 147p on 21 September, within 2% of its 52-week high of 150p and up 29% from its April low of 113.5p; nor would a break-up activist have crossed 9% on 18 September. What the tape shows instead is a 149p-to-142p drift from 8 to 11 September fully given back by 18 September on ordinary volume -- consistent with a handful of holders reading the Australian trade press, not with the information being in the price. Size: APAC was 18% of FY25 like-for-like group net revenue (GBP204.7m) and fell 22.3%, 'predominantly Australia'; Australia alone fell 31.9% and accounts for the whole gap between the -3.1% group decline ex-Australia and the -7.3% including it. Removing it structurally lifts continuing-group organic growth by roughly 3-4pp and lifts margin; against that sit closure costs on top of FY25's GBP9.1m of separately-disclosed items (largely Australian restructuring), cash out rather than in, and an FY27 consensus of GBP221.8m / +3.6% organic that has to come down on the revenue line. That two-sidedness is why the band spans -4.5 to +5.5 and the point estimate is only +1.2. Net of the rest of the company: this rests on one region, and it requires H1 net revenue and margin to be at least in line, which the 11 June AGM update (Jan-Apr, LFL net revenue in line and supportive of the full year outlook) and an easy cost comparative support -- H1 2025 LFL operating margin was 9.9% after first-half-weighted investment in senior talent that has since annualised, and group central costs fell from GBP12.4m to GBP6.1m.
findings.independence: Independently reported the same day by Mumbrella ('M&C Saatchi is preparing to exit Australia, ending a 30-year run'; 'the Australian business will be folded by November'; 'Woolworths will be the last remaining client ... with its contract ending in November') at https://mumbrella.com.au/mc-saatchi-australia-set-to-close-936541 , and by Campaign Brief Asia at https://campaignbriefasia.com/2026/09/09/mc-saatchi-australia-new-zealand-advertising-agency-management-buyout-no-longer-proceeding/ . The underlying Australian deterioration is corroborated in the issuer's own primary document: the FY25 preliminary results state 'APAC: Net revenue fell 22.3% as the macroeconomic environment in the core Australia market remained very weak' and 'The Group closed its Australian media buying business in September 2025' -- https://www.mcsaatchiplc.com/~/media/Files/M/mc-saatchi/documents/result-centre/2025/fy-2025-results-announcement.pdf

findings.finding: A TR-1 published at 17:25 on 21 September 2026 -- after the London close that sets this window's entry price, and 13.5 hours before the results RNS -- discloses that Harwood Capital / Rockwood Strategic / Oryx (all controlled by Christopher Mills) crossed 9% on 18 September, taking the holding to 9.0865% / 10,907,000 shares from 9,700,000 shares at the 11 June notification. Harwood has been publicly urging a BREAK-UP of M&C Saatchi since March 2026 and has stepped its stake up four times this year: 6.001% -> 7.118% (8 May) -> 8.023% (11 June) -> 9.0865% (18 September).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior instance of a 9%-threshold TR-1 from this holder landing on the eve of a results print for this issuer, so there is no direct history. What there is: the three previous Harwood step-ups (12 May, 15 June, 5 August window) landed on ordinary days and moved nothing visible, which is the point -- none of them coincided with a catalyst. The comparable line is governance news, and the 9 March 2026 announcement of the CEO's departure with Vin Murria returning as deputy chair was the trigger for a re-rating from 113.5p in April to 150p in September.
findings.original_quote: 5. Date on which the threshold was crossed or reached: 18-Sep-2026. 6. Date on which Issuer notified: 21-Sep-2026. 7. Total positions ... Resulting situation on the date on which threshold was crossed or reached: 9.086500 ... Total number of voting rights held in issuer: 10907000. Position of previous notification (if applicable): 8.023000.
findings.why_not_priced: It was published at 17:25, i.e. after the 16:30 close, so it is not in the entry price by construction -- the baseline's spot was struck at 13:39 UTC. It is also arithmetically a real purchase and not a buyback artefact: the 2,222,500 shares cancelled under the programme only take 9,700,000 shares from 8.023% to 8.081% of the reduced 120,034,965 voting rights, so Harwood genuinely bought 1,207,000 shares between 11 June and 18 September. Against a median 20-day turnover of USD264,728 (about GBP198k, roughly 135,000 shares a day at 146.7p) that is about nine days of the entire market's volume in this stock, and 274,644 shares traded on 21 September against a 20-day median near 135,000. On a GBP174m AIM name with five analysts, a named activist who has publicly demanded a break-up crossing 9% the night before the interims is exactly the fact nobody is positioned for. If it were priced, the register would not be the only place it exists: there is no broker note, no UK article and no wire copy on it, and the FCA short register is a flat 0.20% residual showing no one on the other side.
findings.independence: Harwood's break-up campaign is independently sourced to The Times via QuotedData, 16 March 2026: 'Harwood Capital is also urging the break-up of advertising group M&C Saatchi', with the stake then at 6% -- https://quoteddata.com/2026/03/morning-briefing-liontrust-buys-martin-gilberts-river-global-harwood-pushes-for-mc-saatchi-break-up/ . The board is configured for the same outcome and this is corroborated by a separate document: the FY25 preliminary results say the Group's 'key focus ... is to unlock the intrinsic value of the Company that is not currently recognised' and that 'the Board remains focused on accelerating initiatives to maximise shareholder value', with Vin Murria (who led the 2022 AdvancedAdvT bid for the company) returning as deputy chair and ex-Lazard banker Nick Shott as NED, and no permanent CEO since Zaid Al-Qassab left on 31 March 2026 -- https://www.sharecast.com/news/aim-bulletin/mc-saatchi-ceo-stepping-down-vin-murria-joins-board--21972116.html

findings.finding: The share buyback programme launched on 9 March 2026 was terminated on 15 September 2026 -- seven days before the interims -- having used only GBP2,877,594 of a GBP4.5m authority (2,222,500 shares at an average 131.1p). It ran out of time, not money. With consensus DPS at nil for both FY26 and FY27 and the Board on record at the FY25 results that it 'believes that greater value can be created for shareholders by increasing the share buyback programme rather than through the payment of a dividend', the interim statement is the natural venue for a replacement programme -- and if none comes, the stock's only mechanical bid has just been withdrawn into a print carrying a closure charge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 20 Apr 2026 FY results, which announced the reallocation of the final dividend into an enlarged buyback, produced +3.91% -- the best results-day reaction in the 13-event observed record. The 9 March 2026 launch of the programme itself coincided with the start of the re-rating from the April low of 113.5p. Capital return is the one line this stock has consistently paid up for.
findings.original_quote: Following the above purchase of shares, the Company announces the completion of the Share Buyback Programme, as launched on 9 March 2026, to acquire up to a maximum aggregate consideration of GBP4.5 million, to be terminated on 15 September 2026. In total, the Group repurchased 2,222,500 ordinary shares for a total consideration of GBP2,877,594, representing an average price per share of 131.1 pence.
findings.why_not_priced: The RNS itself is public, so the fact is not hidden -- what is unpriced is the conjunction, which needs a domestic reader to assemble: an authority left 36% unused, terminated on a fixed date one week before results, on a company whose Board has stated in a primary document that it intends to substitute buybacks for dividends, at a point where a fresh authority would normally be announced with the interims. The programme was buying roughly GBP22k a day against GBP198k of market turnover, about a tenth of the volume in the stock, so its removal is mechanically visible in a name this thin. If the market were positioned for a relaunch there would be commentary on it; there is none from any of the five covering brokers that is publicly visible. This is the smallest and the softest of the three findings -- it rests on an inference about what the Board will do, not on a fact about what it has done -- and it is sized accordingly, with a band that crosses zero.
findings.independence: The Board's stated intention is in a different document -- the FY25 preliminary results: 'the Board intends to reallocate the amount that would otherwise have been proposed as a final dividend for the year ended 31 December 2025' to the buyback, with statutory dividends already at nil (2024: 1.95p) -- https://www.mcsaatchiplc.com/~/media/Files/M/mc-saatchi/documents/result-centre/2025/fy-2025-results-announcement.pdf

outside_window.finding: The physical closure of the ANZ advertising business completes 'by November', with Woolworths the last client to finish, so the cash closure costs, the final headcount exit and any residual impairment land in H2 2026 and are confirmed at the FY26 results, not on 22 September.

FY27 company-compiled consensus of GBP221.8m net revenue / +3.6% organic / GBP31.5m operating profit was struck on 23 April 2026 with ANZ advertising inside the base and has to be reset once the closure is formalised; that reset happens in broker notes over the following days and weeks, not in the 22 September session.

baseline_tension: It agrees, mildly, and that is the main reason the emitted number sits below the sum of the findings: priced_lean_pct is +0.008 which is effectively no statement at all, but run_up_20d_pct +2.23% and run_up_5d_pct +1.87% already lean the way I do, and the short register at 0.20% flat gives me no crowded position to beat -- so two of my three findings are additive to a drift that is already running rather than contrarian to it.
local_pass_note: The domestic pass FLIPPED THE SIGN of the whole hunt, from -2.0 to +2.4. The English pass found the Australia closure and read it the obvious way -- an unannounced country exit disclosed for the first time in an interim statement, sized -2.0 on the memory of the -12.24% reaction to the 2025 interims.

What the domestic pass supplied was the other half of the story, and it is only in domestic documents: the TR-1 record on Investegate shows Harwood Capital stepping from 6.001% to 7.118% to 8.023% to 9.0865% across 2026, and QuotedData (from The Times, 16 March 2026) shows Harwood publicly urging a BREAK-UP. An activist who wants the company broken up, buying more four days before the print and nine days after the Australia closure broke, re-reads that closure as the first execution of the break-up rather than as a fresh disaster. Finding 1 was re-signed from -2.0 to +0.8 (then +1.2 after LESSONS) with a band that still spans -4.5 to +5.5.

Added finding 2 (Harwood 9.0865%, +1.5). This is the single most valuable thing either pass produced and it exists nowhere but the RNS: the TR-1 hit at 17:25 on 21 September, AFTER the close that sets this window's entry price, so it is unpriced by construction.

Added finding 3 (buyback termination 15 September, GBP2.88m of a GBP4.5m authority, +0.4) from the 'Transaction in Own Shares & Buyback Completion' RNS. An English-language search returns the existence of a buyback; only the RNS text says the authority was left 36% unused and the programme killed on a fixed date seven days before results.

The domestic pass also established the NEGATIVE that makes finding 1 a finding at all: the full Investegate announcement list for this EPIC contains no RNS on the MBO, its collapse or the closure, and Sharecast -- which covered this issuer's March 2026 CEO change -- did not carry the September story either.

Honest caveat on the freeze: the mandated event-reality check sent me to Investegate before pre_local was frozen, so I had seen the announcement LIST (not the announcement bodies) when I froze it. pre_local carries only the Australia finding, sized from the Australian trade press alone, which is what the English pass actually produced. The buyback and TR-1 bodies were read only in the domestic pass.

Corrected in the domestic pass: the stake increase cannot be attributed to the last few days. Harwood's 1,207,000 extra shares were bought somewhere between the 11 June and 18 September notifications; only the 9% threshold crossing is dated 18 September. Finding 2 is worded to that limit.
lessons_applied: 'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error. Size on the name's own reaction distribution, not on how certain you are of the fact.' Re-read the 13 observed reactions: the ten events carrying no real news moved 0.0-3.9%, but the two carrying genuine Australia news moved -12.24% and -5.16%. I have genuine, unpriced news of exactly that kind, so finding 1 went from +0.8 [-3.5, +4.0] to +1.2 [-4.5, +5.5] -- the point estimate up a little, the band widened a lot, because the magnitude was the thing I had understated, not the sign.

'Coverage tells you which regime you are in ... at 3-7, nobody is positioned for a confirmed fact, which is the setup for a large move.' analyst_band is 3-7 with 5 analysts. Finding 2 is a confirmed fact in a primary regulatory document that nobody can be positioned for, so it went from +1.2 to +1.5 [+0.2, +3.5].

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number.' baseline_tension says my findings agree with the run-up rather than cutting against it, so expected_move_pct is +2.4 against a finding sum of +3.1 -- 0.7 points smaller, taken off finding 1 because that is where the two-sidedness lives.

'A one_off with no stated path to the guide is sized at a fraction.' Kept finding 1 filed as guidance rather than one_off, and made the path explicit: the closure removes the whole of the gap between the -3.1% group decline ex-Australia and the -7.3% including it, which is a change to the forward organic and margin profile, not just a closure charge.

'Net of the rest of the company.' Added to finding 1 what has to go right in the other ~90% of net revenue for it to be worth anything -- H1 in line, which the 11 June AGM update and the annualising first-half-weighted 2025 cost base support -- and sized it net of that.

'Keep findings inside the exit window ... here the window is one session.' Moved three items out of findings into outside_window: the November physical closure, the FY27 consensus reset, and the permanent-CEO appointment. That removed 1.8 points of negative and 1.0 of positive from the ranked sum.

'Two findings resting on one document are one finding.' Checked: the three rest on three different documents (Campaign Brief 9 Sep, TR-1 21 Sep, buyback RNS 15 Sep). The FY25 preliminary results PDF is used as corroboration in all three but is load-bearing in none, which is stated in each independence field.

'Read the URL strictly.' Re-verified every date off the URL path or the document header rather than the snippet: campaignbrief.com header 'September 9 2026, 1:25 pm', campaignbriefasia /2026/09/09/, quoteddata /2026/03/, Investegate document dates 15 and 21 September 2026.

'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with.' The 0.20% short register is a residual with nothing to beat, so I said so plainly in positioning_check rather than treating it as evidence of anything, and made clear the live positioning fact on this name is a long one.
Dropped nothing on the lessons pass -- no rule in the file cut against a finding I held.
